records.text: Enterprise Smart Management System & Automated Lifecycle Documentation Framework
1. Executive Summary & Core Architectural Vision

My Company operates in high-precision automotive electronics and mobility solutions, engineering products such as Body Control Units (BCU), Telematics Systems (SLCT), Xlink Controllers, eFan Controllers, and Power Shuttle Transmissions. To ensure compliance with quality management systems (IATF 16949:2016 and ISO 9001:2015) and environmental standards (ISO 14001), Hexense Labs requires a centralized, fully integrated Smart Enterprise Automation Architecture.
This document specifies the Smart Company Management System (SCMS). The framework unifies all eleven functional departments into a single digital backbone: Project manufacture.

Key Technological Pillars
Departmental Settings & SLA Controls

Every page and lifecycle stage within the system enforces default operational targets, standard timelines, and lead-time benchmarks. Through a centralized settings interface, each department can fully customize its operational baseline, including:
Department-Specific Auto-Drafting Templates: Standardized document definitions, checklists, and forms tailored to departmental outputs.
Roles & Responsibilities Matrix: Granular permission mapping, ownership rules, and sign-off authorities across all functional positions.
WIP & Milestone Tracking Features: Configurable stage gates, tracking fields, automated status updates, and progress metrics.
Standard Timelines & Lead Times: Default Service Level Agreements (SLAs), turnaround targets, and escalation thresholds for all workflow tasks.
Automated Identifier & Document Numbering Engine: Eliminates manual naming errors by dynamically composing standardized document tags across every engineering and commercial output.

Auto-Drafting Master Templates: Automatically generates cross-departmental baseline templates upon project initiation or trigger events, including Commercial Proposals & Quotations, Contract Review Records (HLPL/F/MKT/01), DFMEA sheets, BOM Cost & Compliance Trackers, APQP Checklists (HLPL-APQP-001), Process Flow Diagrams (PFD), Control Plans, PPAP Checklists (F-PUR-15), Supplier Capacity & Scorecards (F-PUR-11/16), First-Piece & PDI Certificates, and Skill Matrix & Training Reports (HLPL/F/HR/03).
Real-Time Cross-Departmental Alert Triggers: Automated notifications via CRM/ERP push updates to webhooks and email when gated lifecycle thresholds are breached or dependencies clear.
Bi-Directional Change Control: Instant synchronization between engineering updates (ECN/ECO), Bill of Materials (BOM) changes, and manufacturing line configurations.
Live OEM Client Portal Integration: Provides direct visibility for OEM partners to review feasibility, sign off on Product Requirement Specifications (PRS), and track production milestones.

records.text: Single Source of Truth: Project Master Spec Sheet (PMSS)

Every newly created project initializes a unified Project Master Spec Sheet (PMSS) within the central database. Upon project creation, the system automatically generates and attaches the APQP Phase Mapping, Risk Management Matrix, department-specific templates, roles and responsibilities matrix, WIP tracking features, and default SLA/timeline baselines to the PMSS core. The PMSS aggregates system-level requirements:
Operating Parameters: System Nominal Voltage (12V/24V), Operating Temperature Range (-40°C to +85°C), Enclosure IP Rating (IP67/IP68), I/O Channel Mapping.
Compliance Requirements: (based on vehicle type)AIS-140, AEC-Q100/Q200 Grade Selection, ISO 7637-2 Pulse Immunity, RoHS/REACH compliance.
Target Metrics: Target Unit BOM Cost, Manufacturing Cycle Time, Target Delivery Dates.

records.text: 3. Complete End-to-End Automated Project Lifecycle Flow
Here are a total of nine stages that you identify as a life cycle, below are details :
Stage 1: Sales Intake & Client Portal Form

Data Inputs: Inbound client inquiry details (contact, target vehicle platform, operating conditions), reference Customer data filling form document link (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YsM3XHDcrL5N0g_jzTmji1h6gYKV6ByH), annual target volume projections, and lead metadata.
Trigger Event: Inbound customer inquiry logged into CRM system (HLPL-F-SAL-01).

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: CRM generates unique Enquiry ID (e.g., 2026-27/001), creates dynamic secure Client Portal Form Link, and dispatches automated Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (HLPL-SAL-mNDA-01) for electronic signature.
Department Notifications: Sales & BD receives lead assignment notification; Legal / Admin alerted to track NDA execution.
Workflow:
Sales Executive logs lead metadata into CRM (HLPL-F-SAL-01).
OEM client completes portal details: Statement of Requirements (SOR), volume projections, target vehicle platform, and operating conditions.
Automated NDA workflow generates and dispatches a Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement for electronic signature.
Stage 2: Cross-Departmental R&D Feasibility Analysis
Data Inputs: Bilaterally signed mNDA, complete customer SOR (voltage levels, pin counts, communication protocols, thermal envelope, target unit cost).
Trigger Event: Full submission of client SOR and execution of mNDA (initiating automated creation of the central PMSS).

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: System initializes draft PMSS (HLPL-[PROJ]-PMSS-00), automatically attaching the APQP Phase Mapping, Risk Management Matrix, auto-drafting master templates, roles and responsibilities matrix, milestone tracking features, and SLA/timeline baselines, generates Contract Review Record (HLPL/F/MKT/01), and creates review tickets across R&D domains.
Department Notifications: R&D Leads (Hardware, Firmware, Software, Mechanical), Purchasing Lead, Quality Lead, and Sales Lead receive review task tickets.
Workflow:
Hardware Feasibility: Evaluates voltage levels, pin counts, controller processing power, and sensing interfaces.
Software/Firmware Feasibility: Assesses protocol stacks (CAN, J1939, MQTT), memory footprint, and cloud data throughput.
Mechanical Feasibility: Evaluates packaging constraints, connector orientation, and thermal dissipation envelope.
Purchasing & Commercial Feasibility: Verifies component availability, lead times, and preliminary unit costs against target margins.
Contract Review Execution: Formal completion of Contract Review Record (HLPL/F/MKT/01) with cross-functional sign-offs.
Stage 3: Requirement Freeze & Commercial Confirmation
Data Inputs: Approved Contract Review Record (HLPL/F/MKT/01), validated PMSS parameters, target unit price, development NRE quotes, and delivery schedule.
Trigger Event: Multi-department feasibility sign-off completion on Contract Review Record.

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: System compiles Product Requirement Specification (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-PRS-00) and Commercial Proposal & Quotation (HLPL-SAL-QUO-01), routing them to the OEM via the Client Portal.
Department Notifications: Sales Lead alerted to transmit proposal; Accounts Lead notified to expect incoming PO/LOI.
Workflow:
Sales transmits commercial proposal and frozen PRS to the client via the Client Portal.
Client signs PRS digitally and issues Purchase Order (PO) or formal Letter of Intent (LOI).
Accounts verifies PO details against quotation terms.
Stage 4: Proof of Concept (POC) by Hardware, firmware & software(if applicable) & Live Client Portal Sync
Data Inputs: Verified customer Purchase Order/LOI, frozen PRS-00, pinout specifications, block diagrams, MCU driver libraries.
Trigger Event: Account verification and PO lock in ERP core.

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: System initializes project workspace across HW Tracker (HW_01–HW_37) and SDLC (G0–G11), generating Block Diagram (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-BLK-01) and PoC Firmware Test Code (HLPL-[PROJ]-ESW-POC-01).
Department Notifications: R&D Engineering leads (HW, FW, SW) notified of project activation; OEM Client Portal team alerted to sync milestone dashboard.
Workflow:
Hardware releases Block Diagram (HW_04) and Power Distribution Tree.
Firmware releases PoC test code for core MCU peripheral validation (HW_12).
Engineering builds bench PoC setup to validate critical circuit functionality.
Automated portal sync updates live project completion percentage visible to OEM client.
Stage 5: Pilot Build & Tentative Deliverables
Data Inputs: Validated bench PoC test results, preliminary schematics, component candidate data, mechanical enclosure dimensions.
Trigger Event: PoC functional clearance and MCU peripheral driver sign-off (HW_12 = OK).

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: Releases Tentative BOM (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-BOM-00), Schematics (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-SCH-01), Layout Files (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-PCB-01), 3D STEP Enclosure Model by soft tooling (HLPL-[PROJ]-MECH-CAD-01), and fires Procurement Request (HW_07).
Department Notifications: Purchasing Lead alerted for sample procurement; Manufacturing/SMT Lead notified to schedule pilot line run.
Workflow:
Automated Procurement Request (HW_07) fires to Purchasing for prototype component sourcing.
Purchasing orders sample parts, bare PCBs, panel stencils, and 3D enclosure prints (HW_08, HW_26).
Prototype SMT assembly (HW_30, HW_31) executed in-house or via empanelled job-work vendors.
Hardware conducts basic bring-up and verification (HW_31).
Stage 6: Client Validation & Pre-Compliance Testing
Data Inputs: Assembled prototype units, Design Verification Report (HW_32 / DVR = OK), pre-compliance test plan, DVP&R test profiles.
Trigger Event: DVR approval with zero critical bugs (HW_32 = OK).
Automated Action & Artifact Generation: Generates Pre-Compliance Testing Checklist (HLPL-[PROJ]-QA-DVP-01), dispatches proto samples to client, and logs field feedback records.
Department Notifications: Quality Assurance Lead notified to oversee testing; Sales Lead notified to track customer field validation sign-off.
Workflow:
R&D conducts internal EMC/EMI and ESD pre-compliance testing based on the DVP&R (HW_27).
Pilot units handed over to client for vehicle fitment and proto testing.
Client submits feedback and field validation reports via the Client Portal.
If issues are identified, system triggers ECN control loop (HW_32A / HW_36A).
Stage 7: Final Hardware & Mechanical Design Release
Data Inputs: Signed client proto approval, cleared pre-compliance test reports, resolved ECN/ECO items, finalized software HSI spec.
Trigger Event: Client proto clearance uploaded to portal and internal DVP&R approval.

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: Auto-compiles and freezes Final Gerber Package (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-GER-01), Production BOM (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-BOM-01), HSI Specification (HLPL-[PROJ]-ESW-HSI-01), and 2D/3D Mechanical Release Drawings (HLPL-[PROJ]-MECH-DRW-01).
Department Notifications: R&D Head receives approval gate ticket; Purchasing and Quality Leads alerted for production enablement.
Workflow:
Hardware releases Final Gerber Files (HW_24), Production BOM (HW_19), and Hardware-Software Interface (HSI) spec (HW_28).
Mechanical freezes 2D engineering drawings and injection mold tooling CAD models (HW_17).
Quality compiles final Design Verification Plan and Report (DVP&R).
Release Package uploaded to central repository under strict role-based access.
Stage 8: Type Approval & Long-Range Supply Chain Planning
Data Inputs: Frozen Production BOM-01, annual volume forecast, vendor desktop evaluations, supplier capacity figures.
Trigger Event: R&D Head sign-off on Stage 7 Release Package (HW_26 Release Gate).

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: Generates Desktop Supplier Evaluation (F-PUR-10), Capacity Assessment (F-PUR-16), Supplier PPAP Dossiers (F-PUR-15), Approved Supplier List update (HLPL-PUR-ASL-01), and TAC / AIS-140 compliance filings.
Department Notifications: Purchasing Lead alerted to execute long-lead POs; Regulatory/Quality Lead alerted for TAC certification tracking.
Workflow:
Purchasing executes Desktop Supplier Evaluation (F-PUR-10) and Capacity Assessment (F-PUR-16) for volume suppliers.
Parts cataloged into Category A (Automotive Grade AEC-Q) and Category B (Standard Grade with DFMEA waiver).
Quality oversees supplier PPAP submissions (F-PUR-15) and audits.
Regulatory team secures official AIS-140 / TAC certifications.
Stage 9: Mass Production, EOL Testing & Logistics
Data Inputs: Customer mass production PO, active ASL/ACML status, production schedule, raw material IQC pass logs, EOL test specifications.
Trigger Event: Customer mass production PO release and ASL component qualification.

Automated Action & Artifact Generation: System generates Production Work Orders, imports Process Flow Diagram ([PROJ]-PFD-01), PFMEA (SS-[PROJ]-02), Control Plan (HLPL-[PROJ]-CP-01), generates serialized PDI Test Certificates, and produces Tax Invoices/e-Way Bills.
Department Notifications: Manufacturing Lead, Testing/PDI Lead, Quality Lead, and Finance/Logistics Lead alerted for dispatch release.
Workflow:
Incoming Quality Control (IQC) inspects raw materials against specs.
SMT Line executes PCB Baking, Solder Paste Printing, SPI, Surface Mounting, Reflow, and AOI inspection.
Through-Hole insertion, Wave Soldering, and Conformal Coating executed.
Automated End-of-Line (EOL) Testing Jig flashes production code, executes functional pin testing, and records pass/fail telemetry to server.
Pre-Dispatch Inspection (PDI) generates serialized QR code labels.
ERP generates Tax Invoice, dispatches shipment, and tracks delivery.

Dual-Track Procurement Engine Architecture
To support both rapid development agility and scalable volume manufacturing, Purchasing & SCM operates a structured dual-track procurement process:

Prototype / Pilot Track: Optimized for speed, rapid iteration, and quick-turn turnaround. Utilizes Tentative BOMs (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-BOM-00), 3D-printed enclosure prototypes or soft tooling, quick-turn bare PCB fabrication, and sample purchase orders for rapid bench-top validation and prototype assembly.

Mass Production Track: Optimized for long-term component availability, strict cost targets, and automotive compliance. Utilizes frozen Production BOMs (HLPL-[PROJ]-EHW-BOM-01), hardened multi-cavity injection molds, panelized production Gerber sets, formal Supplier PPAP Level 3 submissions (F-PUR-15), and long-range material forecasting via ASL/ACML vendor networks.

5. Cross-Departmental Bi-Directional Change Control Loops
To handle engineering changes, field issues, and requirement adjustments, the system enforces four automated, bi-directional closed loops.
Loop 1: Customer Scope / Requirement Change
Trigger: OEM Client submits modified specification via Client Portal.
Automated Action: System flags PMSS as Under Amendment and halts active phase gate transitions.
Routing: Sales receives alert -> R&D (EHW, ESW, MECH) performs impact analysis on BOM, schedule, and tooling.

Resolution: System updates Contract Review (HLPL/F/MKT/01) with amendment details -> Sales issues revised commercial quotation -> Client signs via portal -> PMSS unlocks with incremented revision (e.g., Rev 01 to Rev 02).
Loop 2: Mechanical / Component Interference
Trigger: Automated 3D STEP clearance check detects physical clash between PCB component and enclosure housing.
Automated Action: System generates Mechanical ECO ticket (HLPL-MECH-ECO) linking Hardware placement file and Mechanical assembly.
Routing: Hardware Lead notified -> PCB component repositioned or alternate component package selected (HW_18, HW_20).
Resolution: DFM/DFA check re-executed -> Mechanical re-validates 3D assembly -> Layout re-cleared (HW_23 = OK) -> Updated Gerber files generated (HW_24).
Loop 3: Test Verification Failure
Trigger: Pre-compliance EMC/ESD failure or DVP test failure logged during Stage 6 (HW_32 = NOT OK).
Automated Action: System locks Phase Gate transition, preventing pilot release, and logs Hardware Issues / RCA record (Phase 4).
Routing: Automated escalation to Hardware Lead and Quality Head -> Circuit modification initiated.

Resolution: Hardware modifies Schematic design (HW_15 / HW_32A) -> ECN raised (ECN-001 / ECN-002) -> Prototype re-fabricated and tested -> Re-validation report attached (APQP Item 20) -> Gate unlocked.
Loop 4: Post-Release ECO/ECN
Trigger: Component End-of-Life (EOL), cost-reduction drive, or field issue triggers change request (HW_36 / HW_36A).
Automated Action: R&D Head initiates formal Engineering Change Order (ECO) workflow.
Routing:
R&D re-assesses DFMEA RPN scores.
Purchasing checks inventory scrap liability and ASL vendor status.
Quality updates PFMEA (SS-[PROJ]-02) and Control Plan (HLPL-[PROJ]-CP-01).
Resolution: Final sign-off by R&D Head and VP Operations -> ERP automatically updates Active BOM -> SMT line feeder setup sheets updated -> Old revision components locked in inventory.

records.text: 7. Comprehensive Maintenance & Tooling Management Framework

To ensure operational continuity across SMT lines, automated testing jigs, and mechanical fabrication equipment, Hexense Labs enforces a Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) master plan integrated with strictly monitored mean-time metrics and quality assurance registers.
7.1 Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) Master Plan & MTBF/MTTR Tracking

Preventive and predictive maintenance schedules are executed according to the enterprise TPM plan. Equipment performance is monitored against key maintenance benchmarks to eliminate unplanned line stops and process drift:

Preventive Maintenance (PM) Cycles: Biannual and annual preventive servicing covering PCB loaders, automatic solder paste printers, SPI units, chip shooters, reflow ovens, AOI units, wave soldering machines, and automated EOL jigs.
Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) & Mean Time to Repair (MTTR): Tracked per machine to evaluate Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and optimize spare parts inventory.
Autonomous Maintenance & Start-Up Checks: Daily start-up verification checklists executed by machine operators prior to batch production runs.
7.2 Calibration Registers (IMTE) & Measurement System Analysis (MSA / Gage R&R)

All Inspection, Measuring, and Test Equipment (IMTE) used across quality control and production lines are subject to strict calibration controls and Measurement System Analysis (MSA) under IATF 16949 requirements:

IMTE Calibration Register: Centralized tracking of dial vernier calipers, micrometers, multimeters, and oscilloscopes, maintaining national/international traceability standards and calibration expiration alerts.

Gage Repeatability & Reproducibility (Gage R&R): Statistical studies conducted periodically for all measurement systems identified in Control Plans to validate gauge accuracy, operator consistency, and process capability.
7.3 Customer-Owned Tooling Tagging, Care, Custody & Insurance Control
Customer-owned assets, including stencils, molding dies, fixtures, and consigned materials, are systematically controlled to prevent damage, loss, or unauthorized modification:
Identification & Tagging: Physical tagging and register logging detailing customer name, part mapping, location, condition, and life counts.
Insurance & Liability Coverage: Verification of property insurance covering customer-owned assets in the company's care, custody, and control.
Program & Data Backup: Offsite access-controlled repository storing CNC code, pick-and-place files, stencil artwork, and test scripts with annual restoration tests.
7.4 Power & Utility Contingency Drills
To prevent production loss, data corruption, or SMT oven board scrap during grid power disruptions, annual contingency drills validate backup utility systems:
DG & UPS Load Testing: Quarterly load tests of diesel generators and UPS units supporting SMT lines, reflow ovens, MES servers, and HVAC systems.
Functional Outage Drills: Simulated extended outage drills testing automatic DG start, graceful MES shutdown, reflow oven restart verification, and first-article product validation.
8. Advanced HR People Management, Operations & Competency Framework
8.1 Annual Skill Matrix Evaluations (HLPL/F/HR/03)
Departmental competency is assessed annually across all 11 functional units using standardized evaluation procedures (HLPL/F/HR/03):
Rating Methodology: Employees are scored across 8 key domain skills on a 1–4 scale (1 = Learner, 2 = Under Supervision, 3 = Independent, 4 = Expert/Trainer).

Competency Thresholds: Overall scores determine employee classification into Level 1 (<25%), Level 2 (26–50%), Level 3 (51–75%), and Level 4 (76–100%). Employees with skill gaps below the required department level trigger mandatory training interventions.
8.2 Training Need Identification (TNI) & Training Effectiveness Tracking
Employee development is managed through structured identification and evaluation loops:
TNI Workflow: Skill matrix gap reports, customer complaint trends, and new tool onboarding automatically populate the Annual Training Plan.
Effectiveness Evaluation: Post-training practical tests, re-assessment after 30 days, and work performance monitoring confirm skill acquisition before closing training tickets.
8.3 Statutory Compliance Calendar, BGV Records & Grievance Registers
Administrative and legal compliance workflows maintain complete oversight of employee lifecycle records and corporate governance:
Statutory Compliance Calendar: Automated 90-day alert tracking for factory licenses, pollution consents, fire safety clearances, and labor compliance filings.
Background Verification (BGV): Mandatory credential, criminal, and previous employment verification for all onboarding personnel retained in HR archives.
Grievance & Query Tracking: Centralized registers logging employee grievances, resolution timelines, and whistle-blower complaints.
8.4 Six Sigma DMAIC Deployment Integration
Operational excellence drives continuous improvement through cross-functional Six Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) project deployment:
Roadmap & Tollgate Reviews: Scheduled phase reviews ensuring DMAIC project alignment with departmental KPIs and First-Pass Yield targets.
Training & Certification: Structured Belt training integrated into HR skill matrices to build problem-solving capability across manufacturing and engineering teams.
9. Master Document Inventory & Departmental Artifacts Annexure

This section outlines the comprehensive baseline index of all standard operating procedures, policies, quality forms, registers, and software development lifecycle artifacts governing the Enterprise Smart Management System across departments. Each departmental inventory is structured into three distinct categories: (1) Common Departmental & Operational / Maintenance Documents, (2) Periodic & Conditional Operational Reviews (including monthly checklists, scheduled audits, and time-bound compliance reviews), and (3) Project-Specific Deliverables & Artifacts.
